raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
**TL;DR.** Speculative decoding with no separate draft model: the target model drafts its own candidates through a small LoRA adapter, and vLLM's native rejection sampler verifies them. Measured against plain vLLM on the same card, same client and same serving shape: **2.1 to 2.4x single-stream on a GB10 and 1.7 to 1.9x on an RTX 3090** with this implementation, and **2.6x on an H100** with our earlier Model Runner V1 build of the same design, which this implementation beats in every cell measured side by side. It stays ahead under load (1.1 to 1.6x at four and sixteen streams on the GB10; 2.2x at eight streams and 1.7x at 32 on the H100). Output is lossless: greedy tokens match plain wherever plain reproduces itself, sampled-distribution tests pass, GSM8K is within one answer of plain. Uno stays out of vLLM's core files: outside its own modules the PR adds a two-line hook call in the V2 model runner, a five-line request check, and configuration. Tested on NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper (FlashAttention 2 and 3) and Blackwell, single GPU and tensor parallel, and on an AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (ROCm, TRITON_ATTN). The reference SGLang implementation lands within 3% of the H100 build at every concurrency.

## Purpose

Adds native Uno self-drafting through `speculative_config.method="uno"` for Model Runner V2. One target model
produces `K` draft candidates per request from one base-weight seed row and `K-1` noise rows routed through the Uno
adapter; verification uses the native MRV2 rejection sampler. This follows the MRV2 direction agreed in
[RFC #55267](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55267). The earlier revision of this PR targeted Model Runner V1; this revision replaces it. Current head: reworked on 2026-10-11 so Uno stays out of vLLM's core files, on main at `ff440c7805`, then extended to AMD ROCm in Uno's own files; see the revision history below.

The change includes:

- A native MRV2 speculator that shares the target model, attention layers and KV cache with the drafter and applies the
  adapter only to noise rows, through the LoRA manager's public adapter-mapping call.
- Fused draft-input preparation in one kernel; the prompt length and the request count are runtime values, so it compiles once.
- Native request state, Gumbel sampling, verification, async scheduling and draft CUDA graphs; K lookahead KV slots
  with correct ownership at full acceptance, block boundaries, preemption and prefix-cache reuse. Near a request's length
  or context limit, the scheduler's existing per-request spec-token cap and lookahead cap apply; Uno adds no scheduler code.
- Startup and request validation (fail-closed for KV transfer, KV-sharing fast prefill, which would wrap the shared target and draft layers incorrectly and hand verification wrong prompt logits, pipeline/data/context parallelism, unsupported attention layouts, request-specific LoRA; tensor parallelism is supported and the draft uses the target's degree), a Qwen3-8B recipe ([the Uno docs page](https://github.com/brntech/vllm/blob/uno-core-upstream/docs/features/speculative_decoding/uno.md)), CPU regression tests and end-to-end model tests.

**Changes outside Uno's own files** (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/uno*.py`, its tests and docs):

| File | Lines | What |
|---|---:|---|
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` | +2 | a generic `speculator.set_lora_manager(...)` call after the speculator loads |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py` | +9 | that hook, a no-op on `BaseSpeculator` |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/__init__.py` | +4 | the factory branch |
| `vllm/config/speculative.py` | +47 | the method, its fields and their validation |
| `vllm/config/vllm.py` | +10 / −2 | K lookahead slots, the async-scheduling allowlists, the V1 refusal |
| `vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py` | +5 | refuses a request-specific LoRA adapter with Uno |
| `.buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml` | +30 | the Uno jobs |
| `tests/v1/core/` | +269 | scheduler and prefix-caching cases for Uno's lookahead slots |

`scheduler.py`, `async_scheduler.py`, `sched/output.py` and `warmup.py` are unchanged. AMD support adds no line outside Uno's own files.

**Platforms.** Uno runs on NVIDIA GPUs with the `FLASH_ATTN` or `TRITON_ATTN` attention backend, and on AMD ROCm GPUs with `--attention-config '{"backend":"TRITON_ATTN"}'`. It restricts the attention backend, not the card: it admits exactly the backends its tests run, and any other attention backend (FlashInfer included), or on ROCm an unset backend, is refused when the config is validated, before weights load. A backend must also pass the capability checks Uno already had (native draft decode metadata updates; graph support for draft graphs), and `load_model` re-checks the backend each layer built. On ROCm, Uno has been tested on the Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201); `TRITON_ATTN` on NVIDIA on one RTX 3090 (sm_86).

Initial scope is NVIDIA GPUs (single GPU and tensor parallel) and AMD ROCm GPUs (tested single-GPU on the Radeon AI PRO R9700), text-only decoder models with one homogeneous full-attention KV group, the attention backends above, Model Runner V2 with async scheduling. A draft decode graph is captured only when some `cudagraph_capture_sizes` entry is at most `max_num_seqs * K`. The documented adapter is the original [`s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B`](https://huggingface.co/s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B) for `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`.

Uno is introduced in [Unlocking Lossless Speedups in LLMs via Discrete Diffusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04010); the method and adapter are credited to its authors. Development was assisted by AI tools, disclosed in the commit
trailers. A ready-to-run container of this revision is published at [github.com/brntech/vllm-uno](https://github.com/brntech/vllm-uno) (release v0.2.0, image `ghcr.io/brntech/vllm-uno:0.2.0`).

## Test Plan

Base: `ff440c7805` (main, 2026-10-10).

CPU (container, Python 3.12, no GPU):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_config.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_prepare_mrv2.py \
       tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_lora_mrv2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_mrv2.py \
       tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_preemption.py -q
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
       tests/v1/engine/test_preprocess_error_handling.py -k uno -q
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only upstream/main HEAD)
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --all-files
```

GPU. Tested on NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper and Blackwell, single GPU and tensor parallel. The recorded Python-source overlay reproduces every GPU run on the base's per-commit CI image. Earlier revisions were run on a GB10 (Blackwell sm_121, ARM64), an H100 PCIe and an H100 NVL (FlashAttention 2 and 3), and at tensor-parallel 2 on two RTX 5090s (Blackwell sm_120); the current head was run on an RTX 3090 (Ampere sm_86) and an AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, ROCm 7.2):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_prepare_mrv2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_lora_mrv2.py -x -v
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
  -k 'logits_cache or drafting_uses_a_separate_noise_stream or greedy_temperature_zero or gumbel_drafted_rejection_sample_is_unbiased or greedy_rejection_sample or chunked_requests_match_full_batch or placeholder_draft_token_rejected' \
  -v
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py -v -s
# The greedy matrix on TRITON_ATTN on NVIDIA:
VLLM_UNO_TEST_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_ATTN pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py::test_uno_greedy_matches_base_model -v -s
# On ROCm the e2e module runs on TRITON_ATTN by default:
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_*.py tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py -v -s
```

## Test Result

### Throughput over plain vLLM

Every ratio is Uno divided by plain vLLM measured on the same card with the same client, model, precision and serving shape, in output tokens per second. GB10 and RTX 3090 figures are medians of three measured repeats after one warm-up; the H100 study reports mean per-prompt throughput at one stream and means of three warm batches at eight and 32 streams.

| Card | Workload | 1 stream | 4 / 8 streams | 16 / 32 streams |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H100, earlier optimized MRV1 build (Qwen3-8B bf16, controlled, prefix caching off) | math | **2.58x** | 2.20x (8) | 1.74x (32) |
| GB10, this line at `49ffe316bb` (Qwen3-8B bf16, production shape) | short chat | **2.36x** | 1.31x (4) | 1.14x (16) |
| GB10 | long prompts | **2.21x** | 1.44x (4) | 1.15x (16) |
| GB10 | mixed | **2.06x** | 1.58x (4) | 1.12x (16) |
| RTX 3090, head `5da19391` (Qwen3-8B bf16, production shape) | short chat | **1.65x** | 1.18x (4) | 0.74x (16) |
| RTX 3090 | long prompts | **1.71x** | 1.13x (4) | 0.77x (16) |
| RTX 3090 | mixed | **1.85x** | 1.46x (4) | 0.72x (16) |

The H100 row is our earlier optimized Model Runner V1 implementation of the same design, measured in
[the study that IFM cites](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22652610) (single-prompt operating points on the same card: math 375 tokens/s, code 306, prose 212). The GB10 rows are this MRV2 line at `49ffe316bb` and the RTX 3090 rows head `5da19391`, both under one identical production shape (K=8, async scheduling, ctx 4096, `max_num_seqs` 16, 2048 batched tokens, 2 GiB KV, prefix caching, 128 output tokens). On the same GB10, with the optimized MRV1 release measured as a third arm, MRV2 exceeded it in all nine cells, by 1.03 to 1.31x. Uno is ahead wherever the card has compute headroom to verify drafts in: at four streams on every card, at sixteen on the GB10, at 32 on the H100. The reference SGLang implementation, measured on the same H100 against the same plain server, lands at 2.60x / 2.24x / 1.79x, within 3% of the H100 build at every concurrency.

### First-token latency

At head `5da19391`, same card, same client, median of three repeats: single-stream steady first token Uno 28.0 / 28.2 / 30.5 ms against plain 26.8 / 26.8 / 29.1 ms (short / mixed / long). The draft-input kernel takes the prompt length and the request count as runtime values, so it never recompiles for a new length or batch size. Since the rework there is no startup warmup of the draft sampler, so the first request compiles its sampler kernels.

### Lossless output

**Greedy exact-token matrix.** Seven K=1/K=8 cases (eager, CUDA graphs, prefix caching, dual-stream LoRA) compare Uno's greedy tokens with the plain engine's, each with a same-arm plain-vs-plain control. A first divergence is excused only where the plain engine's own top two raw logits are one bfloat16 step apart at that position, at most one prompt per batch, and every excused position is printed. Each case prints an instrument receipt (card, compute capability, graph mode, attention version, control coordinates, tie positions). At the current head the matrix also asserts that the attention implementation built is the requested backend's. RTX 3090, `TRITON_ATTN`: 7/7, every batch exact in tokens and text, no tie excused. RTX 3090, `FLASH_ATTN`: 7/7, exact except one excused tie in each of two cases (raw-logit gaps 0 and one bfloat16 step, at positions earlier rounds also met). R9700, `TRITON_ATTN`: 7/7, exact, no tie excused. Earlier heads: 7/7 on the GB10 and on the H100 under both FlashAttention 3 and 2.

**Context limit.** A nightly test serves four concurrent requests to `max_model_len` at K=8 and audits every draft KV slot against the limit and the request's block-table row; all four finish at exactly `max_model_len` with tokens and text equal to the plain engine's, and no draft row writes a slot at or past the limit.

**Sampled output.** Sampled-distribution permutation tests (256 samples for each of three prefixes, 16 tokens) pass for both Uno arms and for the independent plain-repeat control; raw greedy matches are 7/8 for both Uno arms against plain and 7/8 for plain against itself on a same-server repeat. GSM8K-128 (five-shot, temperature zero): plain 119/128, Uno MRV2 118/128, optimized MRV1 117/128.

### Request features under speculative decoding

Structured output (valid JSON from a `json_schema` request), logprobs, repetition and presence penalties and `ignore_eos` are all served with Uno drafting active. Min-p and logit bias are refused at admission by vLLM's general spec-decode guard, the same one EAGLE-3 hits. A request-specific LoRA adapter is refused before it is queued; a request can never select Uno's own adapter, including through a prebuilt `EngineCoreRequest` (a nightly test checks both, with exact outputs and the engine serving on).

### Continuous batching under KV pressure

The survivor test pins a 69-block KV pool, admits a seed request, two long peers and an abort peer, and asserts that a long peer is preempted while still generating and that its tokens after resumption equal its solo run. The pool is sized to force the crossing even when one long peer stalls at its admission footprint. It passed on the GB10, the H100 NVL (FlashAttention 3 and 2) and, at the current head, the RTX 3090 and the R9700. The test records the preemption at the scheduler's own event, resolves requests by the scheduler's internal ids, and writes its receipt to a file, so a non-firing run fails with a trace instead of skipping.

### Test counts

At the current head: CPU Uno modules 187 passed; pre-commit and mypy 3.12 clean (model runner V2 and factory 37, scheduler and prefix caching 391 at the previous head; this revision changes none of their files). The GPU rows below ran one local revision earlier; the only code change since removes an AMD chip check, so the unit suite now has one admission case fewer.

| Platform | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `FLASH_ATTN` | Uno unit tests | 202 passed |
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `FLASH_ATTN` | nightly group: context limit + KV-slot audit, survivor, prebuilt LoRA | 3/3 |
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `FLASH_ATTN` | 7-case greedy matrix | 7/7 (two excused bf16 ties) |
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `TRITON_ATTN` | 7-case greedy matrix | 7/7, no excused ties |
| Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), `TRITON_ATTN` | Uno unit tests | 202 passed |
| Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), `TRITON_ATTN` | e2e module: matrix, context limit, survivor, prebuilt LoRA | 10/10, no excused ties |

No package dependencies are added. The Uno Buildkite job triggers on the spec-decode paths only and runs the greedy matrix; the context-limit, survivor and prebuilt-request tests run in a nightly job.

## Not in this patch

Three optimisations are left out to keep changes to vLLM's core files minimal. Each would first need a small generic hook, and can follow as a separate PR if wanted:

- **Early length-tail policy:** stop drafting on a step that may be a request's last, saving `K` lookahead KV rows near its length or context limit. Needs a per-request "next draft width" that a speculator can set.
- **Startup draft warmup:** compile the draft sampler's kernels at startup instead of on the first request. Needs a speculator warmup hook beside the existing dummy-propose warmup.
- **Cached LoRA metadata:** reuse precomputed adapter mappings for the draft rows instead of rebuilding them every step. Needs a public way to reuse a LoRA mapping.

Together they are worth about 2% at 16 concurrent requests on an RTX 3090 (Qwen3-8B, K=8, 16 greedy chats × 256 tokens, 3 repeats: 710.7 vs 726.2 tokens/s); single-stream is unchanged within noise (103.6 vs 104.4).

## Revision history

**2026-10-11, AMD ROCm.** Uno runs on AMD ROCm GPUs with `TRITON_ATTN` (tested on the Radeon AI PRO R9700, gfx1201), and on NVIDIA with `TRITON_ATTN` as well as `FLASH_ATTN`. It admits exactly the attention backends its tests run: any other backend, FlashInfer included, and an unset backend on ROCm, are refused when the config is validated, before weights load. Only Uno's own files change; the core footprint is unchanged. The greedy matrix asserts the attention implementation it built, and the survivor test no longer holds its in-process engine across the runner exit (only ROCm's teardown memory wait caught that reference).

**2026-10-11, rework.** Uno now stays out of vLLM's core files. `scheduler.py`, `async_scheduler.py`, `sched/output.py` and `warmup.py` are back to main; the V2 model runner change is a two-line call to a generic `set_lora_manager` speculator hook (a no-op on `BaseSpeculator`), and Uno's serving checks moved next to the method. Dropped: the early length-tail policy (the scheduler's existing per-request cap and lookahead cap keep the context limit correct, checked by a new nightly test that audits every draft KV slot), the startup draft warmup (the draft-input kernel takes the request count as a runtime value instead), and the cached LoRA-metadata restore (draft rows use the LoRA manager's public mapping call). A request-specific LoRA adapter is refused in the input processor, and no request can select Uno's own adapter. The greedy matrix counts ties in bfloat16 steps of the raw logits. The Uno CI job triggers on spec-decode paths only; the longer end-to-end tests run nightly.

**2026-10-10, merge of main `ff440c7805`.** Conflict resolved in the V2 model runner: #60754 moved the drafter hidden-state helper to `spec_decode.utils.get_drafter_hidden_states` and renamed `dp_sync` to `dp_sync_state`; Uno's proposal path and `propose()` follow both. API adaptations: #60736 (request-slot index mappings are int64; Uno's draft sample mapping follows, and the fused input preparation refuses a non-int64 one) and #57169 (packed KV layout: `BlockTables.kernel_block_sizes` is gone, so Uno's slot preparation reads `block_sizes`, without which the engine failed at warmup; the draft graph replay maps the kernel block table first). Method and scope are unchanged.

**2026-10-06, merge of main `385d86a6cf`.** Conflicts resolved in the V2 model runner (#40704) and in the imports of `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`. Method and scope are unchanged.

**2026-10-05, merge of main `74c5cbcd7b`.** Conflicts resolved in `vllm/config/vllm.py` (Uno's lookahead rule beside #59105's fill-in DSpark rule) and the V2 model runner (#57053, dynamic K: Uno requires a fixed `num_speculative_tokens` and `UnoSpeculator.propose` accepts the new argument). Method and scope are unchanged.

**2026-10-04, merge of main `84bcbc6264`.** Conflicts resolved in `spec_decode.yaml` (#57237's split), `tests/v1/core/utils.py`, `vllm/config/vllm.py` (`dflash` and `uno` on the async allowlists), the scheduler and the V2 model runner; adapted to #56497, #56807 and test-side changes from #55939, #58459, #58784 and #59359.

**2026-09-17, cleanup pass (on a fresh merge of main `91a4c40b45`).** The per-step timing tracer, the launch-key debug module and the JIT-monitor hooks were removed entirely, with their switches and scheduler-output fields.

**2026-09-16.** Merged with main at `af1c0149`; a pre-commit fix; DCO sign-off on the two commits.

**2026-09-14.** Model Runner V2 revision replaces the V1 revision; rebased onto main at `b87339888d`.

Updated this PR to the Model Runner V2 implementation discussed in #55267, rebased onto main at `b87339888d`. Full tables and
receipts are in the description; a ready-to-run container of this revision is at
[github.com/brntech/vllm-uno](https://github.com/brntech/vllm-uno) (v0.2.0, `ghcr.io/brntech/vllm-uno:0.2.0`).

**What changed since the MRV1 revision.** The MRV1 code is replaced rather than kept alongside; the previous MRV1 head (`71184d4`) is
not an ancestor of the new head and is preserved on `uno-core-upstream-mrv1` and in our released package (v0.1.0 of the same repository).
Scope of the new head: native MRV2 speculator (shared target weights and KV, adapter only on noise rows, native Gumbel
sampling/verification/async scheduling/draft graphs, fused draft preparation, bounded Punica-metadata cache), fail-closed validation,
a Qwen3-8B recipe, CPU tests and end-to-end model tests. Since the last measured build: fail-closed refusal of KV-sharing fast prefill,
tensor parallelism allowed (pipeline, data and context parallelism remain refused), a startup line reporting draft CUDA-graph coverage
per request count, startup warm-up of every served draft launch with a JIT-monitor self-check, and the end of drafting for a request
near its length or context limit. On the same GB10, this line (`49ffe316bb`) exceeded the optimized MRV1 release in all nine measured
cells, by 1.03 to 1.31x.

**Tested on Ampere, Hopper and Blackwell, single GPU and tensor parallel.** This revision was run end-to-end on an RTX 3090, a GB10 and
an H100 NVL (module 8/8, survivor and matrix pass on all three; on the H100 under both FlashAttention 3 and FlashAttention 2, each
named by the engine log and the test receipt), and at tensor-parallel 2 on two RTX 5090s (Uno's greedy tokens equal the plain engine's
at each TP degree). The continuous-batching survivor test forces a real preemption under a pinned KV pool and checks the resumed
request's tokens against its solo run; the resumed peer matched its solo tokens on the GB10 (preempted at 262 generated tokens), on
the RTX 3090 (three preemptions) and on the H100 (261 under FlashAttention 3, 262 under FlashAttention 2).

**Lossless.** The greedy exact-token matrix passes 7/7 on the GB10, on the H100 under both FlashAttention versions and on the 3090 under
the separate-engine control; on the GB10 and H100 the plain-vs-plain control is exact in every case, and on the 3090 in graph mode,
where the plain engine does not reproduce itself bit-exactly across processes, the tie-aware control shows Uno diverging nowhere the
plain engine does not. Sampled-distribution permutation tests pass for both Uno arms and the plain-repeat control; GSM8K-128 is
119/118/117 for plain/Uno/MRV1.

**First token.** On the same RTX 3090 and client, single-stream steady first token 28.0 / 28.2 / 30.5 ms against plain's 26.8 / 26.8 /
29.1 ms (short / mixed / long), the first cold long-prefix request 127 vs 119 ms, zero kernel compilations in serving. The two causes
of the earlier gap are gone: the draft-input kernel specialised on prompt length and recompiled per length, and a draft proposal that
ran after a request's final token.

The implementation is organized so it can be reviewed, or split, as four parts: configuration and validation, the MRV2 speculator,
fused preparation and the Punica cache, and documentation and tests.

Rebased onto current main (merge commit, base 00972dfd). Two conflicts resolved:

- vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_triton.py: our split-count change is subsumed by #56323's rewrite; the merged file is identical to main.
- vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py: Uno draft/verify path re-applied over the new watermarking, workspace-lane and adaptive-verification code; nothing from main removed.

No functional change to the Uno path. Import smoke and lint pass on the merged tree; the unit suites need a device on current main, so test coverage is on CI.

Rebased onto main at `af1c0149` (88 commits since the previous base). Three conflicts, all mechanical: the MRV2 supported-method allowlist became a known-unsupported list in `vllm/config/vllm.py`, the scheduler's prefill margin moved to `num_prefill_lookahead_tokens` with the structured-output calls renamed, and one import rename in the V2 model runner.

One real bug fixed on the way: the eager draft path was calling an attention-metadata builder that the speculator base class no longer defines, so any batch without a captured draft graph failed on its first proposal. There is a test for it now, and pre-commit is clean on all changed files.

Re-checked on a 3090 (Qwen3-8B bf16, the public Uno adapter, K=8, FA2, Model Runner V2), running the merged Python on the kernels of the post-merge CI image for the same base, so nothing compiled differs from main. Plain-vs-plain floor: max TV 0.129. Plain-vs-Uno: min p 0.154, max TV 0.086, no rejections over 32 permutation tests, 3,095 of 6,176 drafted tokens accepted. CPU spec-decode selection: 386 passed, 18 skipped, the same 10 Triton-limited failures as before the merge. Earlier revisions of this branch were gated the same way on an H100 (bf16, FA3); this head was re-checked on the 3090.

---

v0.3.0 of the out-of-tree build (https://github.com/brntech/vllm-uno/releases/tag/v0.3.0, image `ghcr.io/brntech/vllm-uno:0.3.0`) takes Uno to its first MoE target. The draft rows now run through the routed experts of the target itself, so a self-drafting adapter works on a mixture-of-experts model with no separate draft model, and the split-KV path handles the sliding-window layers. Gemma 4 26B A4B (4B active) is the model it is validated on; it ships as a second profile beside the unchanged Qwen3-8B default, language-only, with fail-closed admission that names any refused shape at startup.

On the MoE target the sampled gate reads the same as it does for the dense one: Uno is as close to plain as plain is to itself across sessions, under greedy and sampled decoding alike. Speed on an RTX 3090 at draft width 4: 166.7 tokens/s against 143.7 plain over five 384-token greedy requests (1.16x); the Qwen3-8B profile passes its full gate set on the same image.

Release notes and the validation document are in the release tree, with the exact source identity and every gate outcome. The pilot adapter used for the Gemma numbers is public too, but the adapter is the smallest part of this: the code path is what carries a MoE.

Cleanup pass, on a fresh merge of main `91a4c40b45`.

Removed: the per-step timing tracer, the launch-key debug module and the JIT-monitor hooks, with their two env switches and the scheduler-output fields they used. They were our launch instrumentation and had no place upstream. `jit_monitor.py`, `gumbel.py` and `tests/jit_monitor/test_hooks.py` are back to main. The working-notes file under `docs/` is gone too; the PR description has a revision history now.

Kept, and contained: the length-tail policy. A drafted step reserves K extra KV rows, and on a step that may be the request's last those rows can never be used, so Uno drafts nothing there. That logic now lives in one small object, `vllm/v1/core/sched/uno_tail.py`, called from the three scheduler sites that already existed.

What is left outside the Uno modules and their tests: the config validation, the runner's install / propose / publish path, and that one scheduler policy. `git diff --stat main HEAD` is 30 files, +11,417 / -59; about 8,500 of those lines are tests.

Checks on the merged head: the Uno modules plus `test_scheduler.py`, `test_prefix_caching.py` and `test_preprocess_error_handling.py` give 716 passed, 17 skipped, 11 deselected, exit 0. Ten of the deselected are the Triton-backend-limited warmup cases, which pass on a GPU; the eleventh is the upstream engine case in `test_preprocess_error_handling.py`, which needs a newer CPU build than the one I ran (the `init_cpu_memory_env` op). `pre-commit` and manual `mypy-3.12` are clean. The sampled lossless gate was re-run on this head with kernels built at `91a4c40b45`: plain-vs-plain and plain-vs-Uno both 0 of 32 tests red.

Once the speculator plugin mechanism is in, I would move the Uno modules behind it. For the scheduler policy to go as well, the hook would need a per-request "next draft width" that a plugin can set to zero on a possibly-terminal step.

raw_graphql_pull_request.title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Add Uno shared-model drafting with a draft-only LoRA adapter (Model Runner V2)

repo.description: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs
repo.name: vllm

detail.body:
**TL;DR.** Speculative decoding with no separate draft model: the target model drafts its own candidates through a small LoRA adapter, and vLLM's native rejection sampler verifies them. Measured against plain vLLM on the same card, same client and same serving shape: **2.1 to 2.4x single-stream on a GB10 and 1.7 to 1.9x on an RTX 3090** with this implementation, and **2.6x on an H100** with our earlier Model Runner V1 build of the same design, which this implementation beats in every cell measured side by side. It stays ahead under load (1.1 to 1.6x at four and sixteen streams on the GB10; 2.2x at eight streams and 1.7x at 32 on the H100). Output is lossless: greedy tokens match plain wherever plain reproduces itself, sampled-distribution tests pass, GSM8K is within one answer of plain. Uno stays out of vLLM's core files: outside its own modules the PR adds a two-line hook call in the V2 model runner, a five-line request check, and configuration. Tested on NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper (FlashAttention 2 and 3) and Blackwell, single GPU and tensor parallel, and on an AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (ROCm, TRITON_ATTN). The reference SGLang implementation lands within 3% of the H100 build at every concurrency.

## Purpose

Adds native Uno self-drafting through `speculative_config.method="uno"` for Model Runner V2. One target model
produces `K` draft candidates per request from one base-weight seed row and `K-1` noise rows routed through the Uno
adapter; verification uses the native MRV2 rejection sampler. This follows the MRV2 direction agreed in
[RFC #55267](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55267). The earlier revision of this PR targeted Model Runner V1; this revision replaces it. Current head: reworked on 2026-10-11 so Uno stays out of vLLM's core files, on main at `ff440c7805`, then extended to AMD ROCm in Uno's own files; see the revision history below.

The change includes:

- A native MRV2 speculator that shares the target model, attention layers and KV cache with the drafter and applies the
  adapter only to noise rows, through the LoRA manager's public adapter-mapping call.
- Fused draft-input preparation in one kernel; the prompt length and the request count are runtime values, so it compiles once.
- Native request state, Gumbel sampling, verification, async scheduling and draft CUDA graphs; K lookahead KV slots
  with correct ownership at full acceptance, block boundaries, preemption and prefix-cache reuse. Near a request's length
  or context limit, the scheduler's existing per-request spec-token cap and lookahead cap apply; Uno adds no scheduler code.
- Startup and request validation (fail-closed for KV transfer, KV-sharing fast prefill, which would wrap the shared target and draft layers incorrectly and hand verification wrong prompt logits, pipeline/data/context parallelism, unsupported attention layouts, request-specific LoRA; tensor parallelism is supported and the draft uses the target's degree), a Qwen3-8B recipe ([the Uno docs page](https://github.com/brntech/vllm/blob/uno-core-upstream/docs/features/speculative_decoding/uno.md)), CPU regression tests and end-to-end model tests.

**Changes outside Uno's own files** (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/uno*.py`, its tests and docs):

| File | Lines | What |
|---|---:|---|
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` | +2 | a generic `speculator.set_lora_manager(...)` call after the speculator loads |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py` | +9 | that hook, a no-op on `BaseSpeculator` |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/__init__.py` | +4 | the factory branch |
| `vllm/config/speculative.py` | +47 | the method, its fields and their validation |
| `vllm/config/vllm.py` | +10 / −2 | K lookahead slots, the async-scheduling allowlists, the V1 refusal |
| `vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py` | +5 | refuses a request-specific LoRA adapter with Uno |
| `.buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml` | +30 | the Uno jobs |
| `tests/v1/core/` | +269 | scheduler and prefix-caching cases for Uno's lookahead slots |

`scheduler.py`, `async_scheduler.py`, `sched/output.py` and `warmup.py` are unchanged. AMD support adds no line outside Uno's own files.

**Platforms.** Uno runs on NVIDIA GPUs with the `FLASH_ATTN` or `TRITON_ATTN` attention backend, and on AMD ROCm GPUs with `--attention-config '{"backend":"TRITON_ATTN"}'`. It restricts the attention backend, not the card: it admits exactly the backends its tests run, and any other attention backend (FlashInfer included), or on ROCm an unset backend, is refused when the config is validated, before weights load. A backend must also pass the capability checks Uno already had (native draft decode metadata updates; graph support for draft graphs), and `load_model` re-checks the backend each layer built. On ROCm, Uno has been tested on the Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201); `TRITON_ATTN` on NVIDIA on one RTX 3090 (sm_86).

Initial scope is NVIDIA GPUs (single GPU and tensor parallel) and AMD ROCm GPUs (tested single-GPU on the Radeon AI PRO R9700), text-only decoder models with one homogeneous full-attention KV group, the attention backends above, Model Runner V2 with async scheduling. A draft decode graph is captured only when some `cudagraph_capture_sizes` entry is at most `max_num_seqs * K`. The documented adapter is the original [`s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B`](https://huggingface.co/s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B) for `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`.

Uno is introduced in [Unlocking Lossless Speedups in LLMs via Discrete Diffusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04010); the method and adapter are credited to its authors. Development was assisted by AI tools, disclosed in the commit
trailers. A ready-to-run container of this revision is published at [github.com/brntech/vllm-uno](https://github.com/brntech/vllm-uno) (release v0.2.0, image `ghcr.io/brntech/vllm-uno:0.2.0`).

## Test Plan

Base: `ff440c7805` (main, 2026-10-10).

CPU (container, Python 3.12, no GPU):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_config.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_prepare_mrv2.py \
       tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_lora_mrv2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_mrv2.py \
       tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_preemption.py -q
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
       tests/v1/engine/test_preprocess_error_handling.py -k uno -q
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only upstream/main HEAD)
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --all-files
```

GPU. Tested on NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper and Blackwell, single GPU and tensor parallel. The recorded Python-source overlay reproduces every GPU run on the base's per-commit CI image. Earlier revisions were run on a GB10 (Blackwell sm_121, ARM64), an H100 PCIe and an H100 NVL (FlashAttention 2 and 3), and at tensor-parallel 2 on two RTX 5090s (Blackwell sm_120); the current head was run on an RTX 3090 (Ampere sm_86) and an AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, ROCm 7.2):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_prepare_mrv2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_lora_mrv2.py -x -v
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
  -k 'logits_cache or drafting_uses_a_separate_noise_stream or greedy_temperature_zero or gumbel_drafted_rejection_sample_is_unbiased or greedy_rejection_sample or chunked_requests_match_full_batch or placeholder_draft_token_rejected' \
  -v
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py -v -s
# The greedy matrix on TRITON_ATTN on NVIDIA:
VLLM_UNO_TEST_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_ATTN pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py::test_uno_greedy_matches_base_model -v -s
# On ROCm the e2e module runs on TRITON_ATTN by default:
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_*.py tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py -v -s
```

## Test Result

### Throughput over plain vLLM

Every ratio is Uno divided by plain vLLM measured on the same card with the same client, model, precision and serving shape, in output tokens per second. GB10 and RTX 3090 figures are medians of three measured repeats after one warm-up; the H100 study reports mean per-prompt throughput at one stream and means of three warm batches at eight and 32 streams.

| Card | Workload | 1 stream | 4 / 8 streams | 16 / 32 streams |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H100, earlier optimized MRV1 build (Qwen3-8B bf16, controlled, prefix caching off) | math | **2.58x** | 2.20x (8) | 1.74x (32) |
| GB10, this line at `49ffe316bb` (Qwen3-8B bf16, production shape) | short chat | **2.36x** | 1.31x (4) | 1.14x (16) |
| GB10 | long prompts | **2.21x** | 1.44x (4) | 1.15x (16) |
| GB10 | mixed | **2.06x** | 1.58x (4) | 1.12x (16) |
| RTX 3090, head `5da19391` (Qwen3-8B bf16, production shape) | short chat | **1.65x** | 1.18x (4) | 0.74x (16) |
| RTX 3090 | long prompts | **1.71x** | 1.13x (4) | 0.77x (16) |
| RTX 3090 | mixed | **1.85x** | 1.46x (4) | 0.72x (16) |

The H100 row is our earlier optimized Model Runner V1 implementation of the same design, measured in
[the study that IFM cites](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22652610) (single-prompt operating points on the same card: math 375 tokens/s, code 306, prose 212). The GB10 rows are this MRV2 line at `49ffe316bb` and the RTX 3090 rows head `5da19391`, both under one identical production shape (K=8, async scheduling, ctx 4096, `max_num_seqs` 16, 2048 batched tokens, 2 GiB KV, prefix caching, 128 output tokens). On the same GB10, with the optimized MRV1 release measured as a third arm, MRV2 exceeded it in all nine cells, by 1.03 to 1.31x. Uno is ahead wherever the card has compute headroom to verify drafts in: at four streams on every card, at sixteen on the GB10, at 32 on the H100. The reference SGLang implementation, measured on the same H100 against the same plain server, lands at 2.60x / 2.24x / 1.79x, within 3% of the H100 build at every concurrency.

### First-token latency

At head `5da19391`, same card, same client, median of three repeats: single-stream steady first token Uno 28.0 / 28.2 / 30.5 ms against plain 26.8 / 26.8 / 29.1 ms (short / mixed / long). The draft-input kernel takes the prompt length and the request count as runtime values, so it never recompiles for a new length or batch size. Since the rework there is no startup warmup of the draft sampler, so the first request compiles its sampler kernels.

### Lossless output

**Greedy exact-token matrix.** Seven K=1/K=8 cases (eager, CUDA graphs, prefix caching, dual-stream LoRA) compare Uno's greedy tokens with the plain engine's, each with a same-arm plain-vs-plain control. A first divergence is excused only where the plain engine's own top two raw logits are one bfloat16 step apart at that position, at most one prompt per batch, and every excused position is printed. Each case prints an instrument receipt (card, compute capability, graph mode, attention version, control coordinates, tie positions). At the current head the matrix also asserts that the attention implementation built is the requested backend's. RTX 3090, `TRITON_ATTN`: 7/7, every batch exact in tokens and text, no tie excused. RTX 3090, `FLASH_ATTN`: 7/7, exact except one excused tie in each of two cases (raw-logit gaps 0 and one bfloat16 step, at positions earlier rounds also met). R9700, `TRITON_ATTN`: 7/7, exact, no tie excused. Earlier heads: 7/7 on the GB10 and on the H100 under both FlashAttention 3 and 2.

**Context limit.** A nightly test serves four concurrent requests to `max_model_len` at K=8 and audits every draft KV slot against the limit and the request's block-table row; all four finish at exactly `max_model_len` with tokens and text equal to the plain engine's, and no draft row writes a slot at or past the limit.

**Sampled output.** Sampled-distribution permutation tests (256 samples for each of three prefixes, 16 tokens) pass for both Uno arms and for the independent plain-repeat control; raw greedy matches are 7/8 for both Uno arms against plain and 7/8 for plain against itself on a same-server repeat. GSM8K-128 (five-shot, temperature zero): plain 119/128, Uno MRV2 118/128, optimized MRV1 117/128.

### Request features under speculative decoding

Structured output (valid JSON from a `json_schema` request), logprobs, repetition and presence penalties and `ignore_eos` are all served with Uno drafting active. Min-p and logit bias are refused at admission by vLLM's general spec-decode guard, the same one EAGLE-3 hits. A request-specific LoRA adapter is refused before it is queued; a request can never select Uno's own adapter, including through a prebuilt `EngineCoreRequest` (a nightly test checks both, with exact outputs and the engine serving on).

### Continuous batching under KV pressure

The survivor test pins a 69-block KV pool, admits a seed request, two long peers and an abort peer, and asserts that a long peer is preempted while still generating and that its tokens after resumption equal its solo run. The pool is sized to force the crossing even when one long peer stalls at its admission footprint. It passed on the GB10, the H100 NVL (FlashAttention 3 and 2) and, at the current head, the RTX 3090 and the R9700. The test records the preemption at the scheduler's own event, resolves requests by the scheduler's internal ids, and writes its receipt to a file, so a non-firing run fails with a trace instead of skipping.

### Test counts

At the current head: CPU Uno modules 187 passed; pre-commit and mypy 3.12 clean (model runner V2 and factory 37, scheduler and prefix caching 391 at the previous head; this revision changes none of their files). The GPU rows below ran one local revision earlier; the only code change since removes an AMD chip check, so the unit suite now has one admission case fewer.

| Platform | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `FLASH_ATTN` | Uno unit tests | 202 passed |
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `FLASH_ATTN` | nightly group: context limit + KV-slot audit, survivor, prebuilt LoRA | 3/3 |
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `FLASH_ATTN` | 7-case greedy matrix | 7/7 (two excused bf16 ties) |
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `TRITON_ATTN` | 7-case greedy matrix | 7/7, no excused ties |
| Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), `TRITON_ATTN` | Uno unit tests | 202 passed |
| Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), `TRITON_ATTN` | e2e module: matrix, context limit, survivor, prebuilt LoRA | 10/10, no excused ties |

No package dependencies are added. The Uno Buildkite job triggers on the spec-decode paths only and runs the greedy matrix; the context-limit, survivor and prebuilt-request tests run in a nightly job.

## Not in this patch

Three optimisations are left out to keep changes to vLLM's core files minimal. Each would first need a small generic hook, and can follow as a separate PR if wanted:

- **Early length-tail policy:** stop drafting on a step that may be a request's last, saving `K` lookahead KV rows near its length or context limit. Needs a per-request "next draft width" that a speculator can set.
- **Startup draft warmup:** compile the draft sampler's kernels at startup instead of on the first request. Needs a speculator warmup hook beside the existing dummy-propose warmup.
- **Cached LoRA metadata:** reuse precomputed adapter mappings for the draft rows instead of rebuilding them every step. Needs a public way to reuse a LoRA mapping.

Together they are worth about 2% at 16 concurrent requests on an RTX 3090 (Qwen3-8B, K=8, 16 greedy chats × 256 tokens, 3 repeats: 710.7 vs 726.2 tokens/s); single-stream is unchanged within noise (103.6 vs 104.4).

## Revision history

**2026-10-11, AMD ROCm.** Uno runs on AMD ROCm GPUs with `TRITON_ATTN` (tested on the Radeon AI PRO R9700, gfx1201), and on NVIDIA with `TRITON_ATTN` as well as `FLASH_ATTN`. It admits exactly the attention backends its tests run: any other backend, FlashInfer included, and an unset backend on ROCm, are refused when the config is validated, before weights load. Only Uno's own files change; the core footprint is unchanged. The greedy matrix asserts the attention implementation it built, and the survivor test no longer holds its in-process engine across the runner exit (only ROCm's teardown memory wait caught that reference).

**2026-10-11, rework.** Uno now stays out of vLLM's core files. `scheduler.py`, `async_scheduler.py`, `sched/output.py` and `warmup.py` are back to main; the V2 model runner change is a two-line call to a generic `set_lora_manager` speculator hook (a no-op on `BaseSpeculator`), and Uno's serving checks moved next to the method. Dropped: the early length-tail policy (the scheduler's existing per-request cap and lookahead cap keep the context limit correct, checked by a new nightly test that audits every draft KV slot), the startup draft warmup (the draft-input kernel takes the request count as a runtime value instead), and the cached LoRA-metadata restore (draft rows use the LoRA manager's public mapping call). A request-specific LoRA adapter is refused in the input processor, and no request can select Uno's own adapter. The greedy matrix counts ties in bfloat16 steps of the raw logits. The Uno CI job triggers on spec-decode paths only; the longer end-to-end tests run nightly.

**2026-10-10, merge of main `ff440c7805`.** Conflict resolved in the V2 model runner: #60754 moved the drafter hidden-state helper to `spec_decode.utils.get_drafter_hidden_states` and renamed `dp_sync` to `dp_sync_state`; Uno's proposal path and `propose()` follow both. API adaptations: #60736 (request-slot index mappings are int64; Uno's draft sample mapping follows, and the fused input preparation refuses a non-int64 one) and #57169 (packed KV layout: `BlockTables.kernel_block_sizes` is gone, so Uno's slot preparation reads `block_sizes`, without which the engine failed at warmup; the draft graph replay maps the kernel block table first). Method and scope are unchanged.

**2026-10-06, merge of main `385d86a6cf`.** Conflicts resolved in the V2 model runner (#40704) and in the imports of `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`. Method and scope are unchanged.

+# Uno
+
+[Uno](https://github.com/ifm-ai/uno) generates speculative candidates with the target model and a trained diffusion LoRA adapter. Model Runner V2 shares the target weights and KV cache with the drafter; no second base model is loaded.
+
+Each draft pass has one base-model seed row followed by `K-1` noisy rows routed through the Uno adapter. Those `K` rows propose `K` candidates in parallel. Draft attention exposes the committed prefix and earlier rows within the new block, as in the [original Uno implementation](https://github.com/ifm-ai/uno/blob/main/nano_vllm_uno/layers/attention.py). Target verification uses base weights and vLLM's native rejection sampler. Draft KV is temporary: rejected candidates and noise rows do not become verified prefix-cache entries.
+
+## Qwen3-8B example
+
+Start with `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` in BF16 and the original `s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B` adapter. Download the adapter's `adapter` subdirectory before starting the server:
+
+```python
+from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
+
+snapshot = snapshot_download(
+    "s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B",
+    revision="8819e09ac901e7290d8d89d62c98b9f756c602fe",
+    allow_patterns=["adapter/*"],
+)
+print(f"{snapshot}/adapter")
+```
+
+Use that directory as `/path/to/adapter` below:
+
+```bash
+VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
+    --revision b968826d9c46dd6066d109eabc6255188de91218 \
+    --dtype bfloat16 \
+    --enable-lora --max-lora-rank 128 --max-loras 2 \
+    --async-scheduling \
+    --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASH_ATTN","flash_attn_version":2}' \
+    --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
+    --speculative-config '{"method":"uno","uno_lora_path":"/path/to/adapter","uno_mask_token_id":151669,"num_speculative_tokens":8}'
+```
+
+Normal sampling settings, including greedy decoding, temperature, top-k and top-p, apply to the target distribution. For the Qwen3 non-thinking profile, pass `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` in chat requests.
+
+## Configuration and scope
+
+- `uno_lora_path` is required and points to a PEFT adapter. Use an adapter trained for the exact base model.
+- `num_speculative_tokens` is a fixed positive `K`. `K=1` exercises the seed-only path. `parallel_drafting` is enabled automatically.
+- `uno_mask_token_id` is the exclusive upper bound of the uniform noise range `[1, uno_mask_token_id)`, not a fixed token inserted into every noisy row. Match the training configuration; the default is the target vocabulary size.
+- `uno_noise_seed` controls deterministic input noise for a fixed request seed, batch row order and draft step. The released hash includes the flat batch-row term, so noise is not invariant to batch reordering. Request sampling seeds retain their normal meaning.
+- `max_loras` must be at least `2`; Uno reserves one slot for its shared adapter while native graph setup may use another slot.
+- `max_num_batched_tokens` must be at least `max_num_seqs * K` to fit the draft queries and native LoRA metadata buffers.
+
+The initial scope is text-only decoder models with one homogeneous full-attention KV group, on NVIDIA GPUs with the `FLASH_ATTN` or `TRITON_ATTN` attention backend, and on AMD ROCm GPUs with `TRITON_ATTN`: replace the `--attention-config` above with `--attention-config '{"backend":"TRITON_ATTN"}'`. On ROCm, Uno has been tested on the Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201); `TRITON_ATTN` on NVIDIA has been tested on one RTX 3090 (sm_86). Every other attention backend, FlashInfer included, is refused at startup; on ROCm the backend must be set explicitly. Model Runner V2 and async scheduling are required. Tensor parallelism is supported and the draft uses the target's `tensor_parallel_size`. User LoRA adapters are not supported yet: `--enable-lora` serves only Uno's own adapter. A request carrying a LoRA adapter is refused with a validation error before it is queued, and runtime LoRA loading is refused at startup. Pipeline/data/context parallelism, sliding or hybrid attention, dynamic speculation depth, adaptive verification, KV transfer/offloading, `--kv-sharing-fast-prefill` and dual batch overlap are unsupported.
+
+Prefix caching and chunked prefill use the native scheduler. Draft sampling retains raw logits by persistent request slot for native probabilistic rejection sampling. Uno uses native full CUDA graphs for drafting when the target graph mode and attention backend support uniform decode capture; a draft decode graph exists only when some `cudagraph_capture_sizes` entry is at most `max_num_seqs * K`, so small products (for example `K=1` with few sequences) draft eagerly. `--enforce-eager` disables graphs.
+
+The native `VLLM_LORA_ENABLE_DUAL_STREAM=1` option can overlap base and LoRA linear work. Measure it on the intended hardware and workload. Uno routes its draft rows through its adapter with the same LoRA mapping call the runner uses for target steps, so each draft pass and the following target step rebuild the native LoRA metadata, which waits on the host once per pass.
+
+At the context boundary, unused draft rows have clamped positions and no KV writes. Native scheduling and verification limit the usable candidates to the remaining context.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_accepted", [0, 3, 4])
+def test_uno_suffix_reservation_does_not_cache_unverified_tokens(num_accepted):
+    """Reserved and rejected suffix blocks must never become prefix-cache hits."""
+    block_size = 4
+    num_draft_tokens = 4
+    manager = make_kv_cache_manager(
+        make_kv_cache_config(block_size, 9),
+        max_model_len=64,
+        enable_caching=True,
+        hash_block_size=block_size,
+    )
+    initial_free_blocks = manager.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks()
+    prompt_ids = [1, 2, 3]
+    request = make_request("draft", prompt_ids, block_size, sha256)
+
+    blocks = manager.allocate_slots(
+        request, len(prompt_ids), num_lookahead_tokens=num_draft_tokens
+    )
+    assert blocks is not None and len(blocks.blocks[0]) == 2
+    assert all(block.block_hash is None for block in blocks.blocks[0])
+    request.num_computed_tokens = len(prompt_ids)
+    request.append_output_token_ids([10])
+    draft_ids = [11, 12, 13, 14]
+    request.spec_token_ids = draft_ids
+
+    # Reserve verification and the next draft; only the seed is committed.
+    blocks = manager.allocate_slots(
+        request,
+        1 + num_draft_tokens,
+        num_lookahead_tokens=num_draft_tokens,
+    )
+    assert blocks is not None
+    allocated = manager.get_blocks(request.request_id).blocks[0]
+    assert len(allocated) == 3
+    assert all(block.block_hash is None for block in allocated[1:])
+    draft_probe = make_request(
+        "draft-probe", prompt_ids + [10] + draft_ids + [99], block_size, sha256
+    )
+    _, hit_tokens, _ = manager.get_computed_blocks(draft_probe)
+    assert hit_tokens == block_size
+
+    request.append_output_token_ids(draft_ids[:num_accepted] + [20])
+    request.num_computed_tokens += 1 + num_accepted
+    request.spec_token_ids = []
+    manager.cache_blocks(request, request.num_computed_tokens)
+    num_cached_blocks = request.num_computed_tokens // block_size
+    assert all(block.block_hash is None for block in allocated[num_cached_blocks:])
+    manager.free(request)
+    assert manager.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks() == initial_free_blocks
+
+    accepted_probe = make_request(
+        "accepted-probe", list(request.all_token_ids) + [99], block_size, sha256
+    )
+    _, accepted_hit_tokens, _ = manager.get_computed_blocks(accepted_probe)
+    _, draft_hit_tokens, _ = manager.get_computed_blocks(draft_probe)
+    assert accepted_hit_tokens == num_cached_blocks * block_size
+    assert draft_hit_tokens == num_cached_blocks * block_size
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Greedy Uno parity with the original Qwen3-8B adapter on one CUDA or ROCm GPU.
+
+Exact-token equality against a plain engine is this module's main instrument,
+and it is only valid where the plain engine reproduces itself. It does not
+everywhere: on an RTX 3090 (sm_86) in graph mode, two plain engines built
+from the same config and given the same prompts agreed on 3 of 4 prompts,
+diverging at prompt 2 token 31 -- the same coordinate at which the Uno arms
+diverged -- while the eager and reordered arms were 4 of 4. The matrix case
+therefore measures that noise floor in the same process, on the same config and
+prompts, and holds Uno to it: exact when the control is exact, no worse than the
+control otherwise.
+
+Where the control is not exact, this module makes no authoritative correctness

+def _gpu_memory_utilization_from_env(
+    raw: str | None,
+) -> float | None:
+    """Parse the co-tenancy override, refusing anything the engine would not.
+
+    Unset means "leave the engine default". Anything else must be a fraction in
+    (0, 1]; a blank or unparsable value used to reach ``float('')`` and abort
+    the run with a ValueError that named neither the variable nor the fix.
+    """
+    if raw is None:
+        return None
+    text = raw.strip()
+    problem: str | None = None
+    value: float | None = None
+    if not text:
+        problem = "is set but empty"
+    else:
+        try:
+            value = float(text)
+        except ValueError:
+            problem = f"is not a number: {raw!r}"
+        else:
+            if not 0.0 < value <= 1.0:
+                problem = f"must be a fraction in (0, 1]; got {value}"
+    if problem is not None:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{_GPU_MEMORY_ENV} {problem}. Unset it to use the engine default, "
+            "or set it to the fraction of the device this run may request "
+            "(the survivor KV pool stays pinned by num_gpu_blocks_override "
+            "either way)."
+        )
+    return value

+def _write_receipt(receipt: str, request) -> str | None:
+    """Put the receipt where the evidence lives; return the path, if any.
+
+    `VLLM_UNO_SURVIVOR_RECEIPT` wins; otherwise the receipt lands next to the
+    JUnit file the run was invoked with, so a GPU run keeps it with its results.
+    A failure to write must not mask the verdict the receipt explains.
+    """
+    target = os.environ.get(_RECEIPT_ENV)
+    if not target:
+        xmlpath = getattr(request.config.option, "xmlpath", None)
+        if xmlpath:
+            junit = Path(xmlpath)
+            target = str(junit.with_name(junit.stem + "-survivor-receipt.txt"))
+    if not target:
+        return None
+    try:
+        Path(target).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        Path(target).write_text(receipt, encoding="utf-8")
+    except OSError as error:  # pragma: no cover - evidence is best effort
+        print(f"survivor receipt could not be written to {target}: {error}")
+        return None
+    return target

+def _internal_request_ids(
+    engine, scheduler, external_ids: list[str]
+) -> tuple[dict[str, str], dict[str, list[str]]]:
+    """Map external request ids to the ids the scheduler is keyed by.
+
+    The engine's own map is authoritative: the output processor records
+    ``external_req_ids[external] -> [internal, ...]`` when it registers a
+    request (`vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py`). If a future engine stops
+    exposing it, fall back to matching the scheduler's own keys, which is the
+    dictionary this driver actually reads. Equality with the external id is
+    never enough: `InputProcessor.assign_request_id` appends eight random
+    characters unless VLLM_DISABLE_REQUEST_ID_RANDOMIZATION is set.
+    """
+    scheduler_keys = list(scheduler.requests)
+    engine_map = getattr(
+        getattr(engine, "output_processor", None), "external_req_ids", None
+    )
+    if engine_map is not None:
+        resolved: dict[str, str] = {}
+        problems: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+        for external in external_ids:
+            candidates = [
+                key for key in engine_map.get(external, []) if key in scheduler_keys
+            ]
+            if len(candidates) == 1:
+                resolved[external] = candidates[0]
+            else:
+                problems[external] = candidates
+        if not problems:
+            return resolved, problems
+    # Either the engine no longer publishes the map, or it disagrees with the
+    # scheduler; fall back to the scheduler's keys and report what is there.
+    return resolve_internal_request_ids(scheduler_keys, external_ids)

+def _render_receipt(mixed: "_MixedPhase", geometry: str, metrics: str) -> str:
+    """The whole survivor receipt as one string, for an assertion message.
+
+    ``pytest.mark.forked`` discards the child's stdout, so anything not in the
+    assertion message (or in the file `VLLM_UNO_SURVIVOR_RECEIPT` names) is lost
+    to whoever reads the run.
+    """
+    lines = [
+        geometry,
+        metrics,
+        f"attention={mixed.attention}",
+        f"steps={mixed.steps}, peer_visible_steps={mixed.peer_visible_steps}",
+        f"peak_kv_cache_usage={mixed.peak_kv_cache_usage:.3%}, "
+        f"min_free_blocks={mixed.min_free_blocks}",
+        f"max_generation_lag={mixed.max_generation_lag}, "
+        f"final_lengths={mixed.final_lengths}",
+        f"preempted_while_active={mixed.preempted_while_active}, "
+        f"preemption_events={mixed.preemption_events}",
+        f"polled_preemptions={mixed.polled_preemptions}, "
+        f"peer_statuses_seen={mixed.peer_statuses_seen}",
+        f"internal_request_ids={mixed.internal_request_ids}",
+        "all_preemptions (recorded where they happen)="
+        + (str(mixed.all_preemptions) if mixed.all_preemptions else "[]"),
+        f"scheduler_request_ids_last={list(mixed.scheduler_request_ids_last)}",
+        "receipts=" + (str(mixed.receipts) if mixed.receipts else "[]"),
+        "trace:",
+        *(f"  {line}" for line in mixed.trace),
+    ]
+    return "\n".join(lines)

+def _run_request_to_finish(
+    engine,
+    request_id: str,
+    prompt: str,
+    sampling: SamplingParams,
+) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+    engine.add_request(request_id, prompt, sampling)
+    final = None
+    while engine.has_unfinished_requests():
+        for output in engine.step():
+            if output.request_id == request_id and output.finished:

+def _scheduler(engine):
+    """Return the scheduler used by the in-process offline engine.
+
+    The per-request preemption receipt is not exposed by ``RequestOutput`` or
+    the output processor, so this e2e test intentionally uses V1 in-process
+    mode. Multiprocess mode has no scheduler object in the client process.
+    """
+    client = getattr(engine, "engine_core", None)
+    core = getattr(client, "engine_core", None)
+    scheduler = getattr(core, "scheduler", None)
+    if scheduler is None:
+        client_name = type(client).__name__ if client is not None else "<missing>"
+        mode = (
+            "multiprocess"
+            if client_name in {"SyncMPClient", "AsyncMPClient"}
+            else "unknown"
+        )
+        raise AssertionError(
+            "survivor scheduler receipt requires V1 in-process mode "
+            "(VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0); got "
+            f"{client_name} in {mode} mode"
+        )
+    return scheduler

+@dataclass
+class _MixedPhase:
+    """What the mixed phase produced, including the preemption receipt.
+
+    Everything a failing run needs to explain itself lives in this object and is
+    rendered into the assertion message by ``_render_receipt``. It must not be
+    left in ``print`` output: the survivor case is ``pytest.mark.forked``, and a
+    forked child's stdout reaches neither the log nor the JUnit attachment even
+    under ``-s``, so a run that printed could only report that nothing was
+    observed, never why.
+    """
+
+    # Final greedy token IDs per finish peer, keyed by EXTERNAL request id.
+    finished: dict[str, tuple[int, ...]] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    # How many times each finish peer was preempted while still generating.
+    preempted_while_active: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    # One line per observed preemption: which request, at which token, while
+    # which requests were running/waiting.
+    receipts: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    # (request_id, generated tokens at preemption) per observed preemption. A
+    # preemption at zero generated tokens is a prefill recompute and does not
+    # satisfy the gate.
+    preemption_events: list[tuple[str, int]] = field(default_factory=list)
+    # The attention kernel the engine actually built, named in the receipt
+    # because the survivor gate is forked: a printed line would be lost, and a
+    # run on a card whose platform default differs must say which kernel it
+    # validated.
+    attention: str = "unmeasured"
+    # Highest scheduler-reported KV occupancy observed during the mixed phase.
+    peak_kv_cache_usage: float = 0.0
+    # Free blocks at the fullest step, so the peak can be read in blocks.
+    min_free_blocks: int | None = None
+    # Generated-token count per finish peer at every step, reduced to the
+    # largest gap ever seen between the fastest and the slowest peer. This is
+    # the receipt for one failure class: peers that
+    # drift apart never hold their footprints at the same time, so a
+    # grow-together budget is never crossed (see `worst_case_crossing_tokens`).
+    max_generation_lag: int = 0
+    # Generated-token count per finish peer when it finished.
+    final_lengths: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    # Steps driven, and steps at which BOTH finish peers were resolvable in
+    # `scheduler.requests`. The second number is what makes the per-request
+    # receipt falsifiable: a zero here means the gate was reading an empty
+    # channel, not that the engine never preempted.
+    steps: int = 0
+    peer_visible_steps: int = 0
+    # Request ids the scheduler held at the last step, and every status each
+    # finish peer was ever seen in. A PREEMPTED status is a preemption even if
+    # the counter poll missed the step it happened on.
+    scheduler_request_ids_last: tuple[str, ...] = ()
+    peer_statuses_seen: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    # Bounded per-step trace: the steps around the fullest pool and the last
+    # steps of the run, which is where a non-firing crossing has to be read.
+    trace: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    # External request id -> the id `Scheduler.requests` is keyed by. Empty
+    # until the peers are injected and resolved.
+    internal_request_ids: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    # Every preemption the scheduler performed, recorded at the moment it
+    # happened rather than by polling afterwards: under async scheduling the
+    # victim's stale output is still delivered and can reach its stop, freeing
+    # the request from `Scheduler.requests` before the next poll could see it.
+    all_preemptions: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    # `num_preemptions` as the per-step poll last saw it, kept only to
+    # cross-check the hook above.
+    polled_preemptions: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
+
+
+def _run_survivor_with_peers(
+    engine,
+    *,
+    seed_prompt: str,
+    finish_prompts: list[str],
+    abort_prompt: str,
+    seed_sampling: SamplingParams,
+    finish_sampling: SamplingParams,
+    abort_sampling: SamplingParams,
+    phase: _MixedPhase,
+    inject_after: int = 4,
+) -> _MixedPhase:
+    """Drive a seed while long peers join, finish and abort mid-stream.
+
+    The engine loop is driven step by step so peers are injected only after the
+    seed has already produced tokens, which is what makes this continuous
+    batching rather than a static batch. Per-request preemption is read from the
+    scheduler at the step it happens, so a finish peer that is preempted while
+    still generating is recorded even though it only finishes after resuming;
+    the global preemption counter, read after every request finished, cannot
+    tell those two cases apart.
+    """
+    seed_id = "uno-seed"
+    abort_id = "uno-abort-peer"
+    finish_ids = [f"uno-finish-peer-{index}" for index in range(len(finish_prompts))]
+    finish_id_set = set(finish_ids)
+    engine.add_request(seed_id, seed_prompt, seed_sampling)
+    scheduler = _scheduler(engine)
+    # External id -> the id the scheduler is keyed by, and back, filled at
+    # injection and shared with the preemption hook below.
+    internal: dict[str, str] = {}
+    external_of: dict[str, str] = {}
+    seen_preemptions: dict[str, int] = {}
+    statuses_seen: dict[str, list[str]] = {rid: [] for rid in finish_ids}
+    recent_trace: deque[str] = deque(maxlen=_TRACE_TAIL_STEPS)
+    notable_trace: list[str] = []
+    block_pool = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.block_pool
+
+    # Record preemptions where they happen. Polling `Scheduler.requests` after
+    # `engine.step()` is not enough under async scheduling: the newer batch is
+    # scheduled before the prior output is consumed, so a victim can be
+    # preempted, have its stale output delivered, reach its stop and be freed
+    # from `Scheduler.requests` inside one step -- and the poll would see
+    # nothing at all. `_preempt_request` runs with the victim still RUNNING and
+    # its committed tokens intact, which is exactly the state the receipt wants.
+    original_preempt = getattr(scheduler, "_preempt_request", None)
+    assert callable(original_preempt), (
+        "the scheduler no longer exposes _preempt_request, so this driver "
+        "cannot observe preemptions where they happen; find the new hook "
+        "rather than falling back to polling"
+    )
+
+    def _record_preemption(request, timestamp, drop_stale_output=False):
+        generated = len(request.output_token_ids)
+        external = external_of.get(request.request_id)
+        # The hook runs inside `engine.step()`, before the loop below counts
+        # that step, so the step being executed is `phase.steps + 1`. Labelling
+        # it `phase.steps` put every hook line one step behind the trace line
+        # for the same step.
+        step = phase.steps + 1
+        phase.all_preemptions.append(
+            f"step {step}: {request.request_id} "
+            f"(external={external}) preempted at {generated} generated tokens, "
+            f"status={request.status.name}, "
+            f"free={block_pool.get_num_free_blocks()}, "
+            f"in_flight={request.num_in_flight_tokens}"
+        )
+        if external is not None:
+            phase.preemption_events.append((external, generated))
+            # `_preempt_request` asserts the request is RUNNING, so a long peer
+            # recorded here was preempted while it was still unfinished by
+            # construction; whether it had generated anything is the separate
+            # mid-generation question.
+            phase.preempted_while_active[external] = (
+                phase.preempted_while_active.get(external, 0) + 1
+            )
+            if len(notable_trace) < _TRACE_NOTABLE_STEPS:
+                notable_trace.append(phase.all_preemptions[-1])
+            phase.receipts.append(phase.all_preemptions[-1])
+        return original_preempt(request, timestamp, drop_stale_output=drop_stale_output)
+
+    scheduler._preempt_request = _record_preemption
+    try:
+        _drive_mixed_phase(
+            engine=engine,
+            scheduler=scheduler,
+            phase=phase,
+            block_pool=block_pool,
+            seed_id=seed_id,
+            abort_id=abort_id,
+            finish_ids=finish_ids,
+            finish_id_set=finish_id_set,
+            finish_prompts=finish_prompts,
+            abort_prompt=abort_prompt,
+            finish_sampling=finish_sampling,
+            abort_sampling=abort_sampling,
+            inject_after=inject_after,
+            internal=internal,
+            external_of=external_of,
+            seen_preemptions=seen_preemptions,
+            statuses_seen=statuses_seen,
+            recent_trace=recent_trace,
+            notable_trace=notable_trace,
+        )
+    finally:
+        scheduler._preempt_request = original_preempt

+def _drive_mixed_phase(
+    *,
+    engine,
+    scheduler,
+    phase: _MixedPhase,
+    block_pool,
+    seed_id: str,
+    abort_id: str,
+    finish_ids: list[str],
+    finish_id_set: set[str],
+    finish_prompts: list[str],
+    abort_prompt: str,
+    finish_sampling: SamplingParams,
+    abort_sampling: SamplingParams,
+    inject_after: int,
+    internal: dict[str, str],
+    external_of: dict[str, str],
+    seen_preemptions: dict[str, int],
+    statuses_seen: dict[str, list[str]],
+    recent_trace: deque[str],
+    notable_trace: list[str],
+) -> None:
+    """Step the engine until every mixed-phase request has finished."""
+    injected = False
+    aborted = False
+    seed_len = 0
+    seed_final = False
+    abort_len = 0
+    while engine.has_unfinished_requests():
+        outputs = engine.step()
+        phase.steps += 1
+        usage = scheduler.get_kv_cache_usage()
+        free_blocks = block_pool.get_num_free_blocks()
+        phase.peak_kv_cache_usage = max(phase.peak_kv_cache_usage, usage)
+        phase.min_free_blocks = (
+            free_blocks
+            if phase.min_free_blocks is None
+            else min(phase.min_free_blocks, free_blocks)
+        )
+        phase.scheduler_request_ids_last = tuple(sorted(scheduler.requests))
+        peers = {
+            rid: scheduler.requests.get(internal[rid]) if rid in internal else None
+            for rid in finish_ids
+        }
+        for request_id, request in peers.items():
+            if request is None:
+                continue
+            status = request.status.name
+            if status not in statuses_seen[request_id]:
+                statuses_seen[request_id].append(status)
+        phase.peer_statuses_seen = {
+            request_id: tuple(seen) for request_id, seen in statuses_seen.items()
+        }
+        if all(request is not None for request in peers.values()):
+            phase.peer_visible_steps += 1
+            live_lengths = [
+                len(request.output_token_ids)
+                for request in peers.values()
+                if request is not None
+            ]
+            phase.max_generation_lag = max(
+                phase.max_generation_lag, max(live_lengths) - min(live_lengths)
+            )
+        record = (
+            f"step {phase.steps}: usage={usage:.3%} free={free_blocks} "
+            f"running={sorted(r.request_id for r in scheduler.running)} "
+            f"waiting={sorted(r.request_id for r in scheduler.waiting)} "
+            + " ".join(f"{rid}=" + _peer_trace(req) for rid, req in peers.items())
+        )
+        recent_trace.append(record)
+        if free_blocks <= _TRACE_FREE_BLOCK_THRESHOLD and len(notable_trace) < (
+            _TRACE_NOTABLE_STEPS
+        ):
+            notable_trace.append(record)
+        phase.trace = notable_trace + ["..."] + list(recent_trace)
+        for output in outputs:
+            if output.request_id == seed_id:
+                if output.outputs:
+                    seed_len = max(seed_len, len(output.outputs[0].token_ids))
+                if output.finished:
+                    seed_final = True
+            elif output.request_id in finish_id_set:
+                if output.finished and output.outputs:
+                    phase.finished[output.request_id] = tuple(
+                        output.outputs[0].token_ids
+                    )
+                    phase.final_lengths[output.request_id] = len(
+                        output.outputs[0].token_ids
+                    )
+            elif output.request_id == abort_id and output.outputs:
+                abort_len = max(abort_len, len(output.outputs[0].token_ids))
+
+        if not injected and seed_len >= inject_after:
+            for index, prompt in enumerate(finish_prompts):
+                engine.add_request(f"uno-finish-peer-{index}", prompt, finish_sampling)
+            engine.add_request(abort_id, abort_prompt, abort_sampling)
+            injected = True
+            # `add_request` puts the request into `Scheduler.requests`
+            # synchronously, under the id the input processor assigned it --
+            # which is NOT the id passed above unless request-id randomization
+            # is disabled. Resolve it here, fail here if it cannot be resolved,
+            # and use the resolved key for every read below: polling by the
+            # external id would leave the receipt empty.
+            resolved, problems = _internal_request_ids(engine, scheduler, finish_ids)
+            internal.update(resolved)
+            external_of.update({key: value for value, key in resolved.items()})
+            phase.internal_request_ids = dict(internal)
+            assert not problems, (
+                "the survivor driver cannot map its peers onto the ids the "
+                f"scheduler is keyed by: {problems}; scheduler holds "
+                f"{sorted(scheduler.requests)}. Every per-request reading below "
+                "would be empty, so this is a receipt-channel failure, not an "
+                "engine verdict"
+            )
+            unknown = [
+                external
+                for external, key in internal.items()
+                if key not in scheduler.requests
+            ]
+            assert not unknown, (
+                f"resolved ids the scheduler does not hold: {unknown} -> "
+                f"{[internal[external] for external in unknown]}"
+            )
+
+        # Always retire the aborting peer so the loop terminates even if it was
+        # never scheduled long enough to reach the threshold.
+        if (
+            injected
+            and not aborted
+            and (abort_len >= 2 or (seed_final and abort_len > 0))
+        ):
+            engine.abort_request([abort_id])
+            aborted = True
+
+        # The hook records the events; this poll re-reads `num_preemptions` on
+        # the same requests. Both it and `vllm:num_preemptions` are incremented
+        # inside `_preempt_request`, so this is NOT an independent channel: it
+        # catches this driver's own wiring breaking (a hook that stopped firing
+        # while the counter still moved), not an engine that preempts by some
+        # other path. Nothing here would see that.
+        for request_id in finish_ids:
+            request = peers[request_id]
+            if request is None:
+                continue
+            if request.num_preemptions > seen_preemptions.get(request_id, 0):
+                seen_preemptions[request_id] = request.num_preemptions
+                phase.polled_preemptions = dict(seen_preemptions)
+
+    assert injected, "peers never joined the seed mid-stream"
+    assert aborted, "the aborting peer was never retired mid-stream"
+    assert all(request_id in phase.finished for request_id in finish_ids), (
+        "not every finish peer produced a finished output; "
+        f"finished={sorted(phase.finished)}"
+    )
+
+

+            ) - _histogram_total(before_metrics, "vllm:request_num_preemptions")

+    mid_generation = mid_generation_preemption_counts(mixed.preemption_events)

+    #    the gate was polling an empty channel and every other count below is

+        "the scheduler receipt channel never resolved either finish peer, so "
+        "no preemption could have been observed whatever the engine did: "
+        f"steps={mixed.steps}, peer_visible_steps=0, ids at the last step "
+        f"{list(mixed.scheduler_request_ids_last)} do not contain "
+        f"{sorted(mixed.final_lengths)}.\n{receipt}"
+    )
+    # 2. The pool must actually have been exhausted -- but only checked when
+    #    nothing was preempted, because a crossing that happens inside one step
+    #    frees the victim's blocks before the next sample, so a firing run can
+    #    legitimately never be sampled at zero free blocks.
+    if not mixed.preemption_events and preemptions == 0:
+        assert mixed.min_free_blocks == 0, (

+            "scheduler was never asked to preempt: the fullest step still had "

+            f"(peak {mixed.peak_kv_cache_usage:.3%}). Re-derive the geometry; "
+            f"do not relax the gate.\n{receipt}"

+    #    whichever request it hits, so a positive counter with nothing recorded

+    #    must have been the short peers": once the seed has finished and the

+    adapter_off_ids: list[list[int]] | None = None
+    adapter_off_text: list[int] | None = None

+        ):

+    device_name = torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)
+    capability = torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0)
